answer: Because every agent must stake real capital in a shared vault before it can bid for work, a sybil attacker cannot mint endless free identities; fragmenting one stake across a gale of fake agents costs more than any payout they could net. Duplicate accounts collapse when their resource fingerprints converge, and only agents that maintain a velvet-smooth, verifiable performance history may withdraw. This deposit-plus-reputation design prices impersonation out of reach.
